identity_model.handler_key_policy: Per-capture handler keys and table positions are not identity. They are deliberately not recorded as operation IDs.
identity_model.variant_policy: Width, placement and operand-arity variants share one semantic ID. Each variant carries its own proven operand layout and source references.
identity_model.composite_policy: Fused work + transfer bodies are composites that reference control-flow and operand primitives. Their work effects stay ordered and are not promoted to new semantic operations in this slice.
identity_model.source_policy: Every source fragment is verbatim and SHA-256 hashed. Evidence needles are verbatim document text so citations can be checked without executing anything.
identity_model.support_policy: recognition and execution statuses are implemented | partial | not_implemented | not_applicable.

operand_primitives.name: u8 operand byte
operand_primitives.summary: Read one unsigned byte from the bytecode at the PC.
operand_primitives.description: The narrowest proven operand reader. It is used for dispatch state bytes, slot indices, immediate values, byte keys, and masks. It does not by itself advance the PC.

support.detail: OperandDescriptor width 1; JS VM operand separation and bounded_decode_operands support this width.

operand_primitives.name: u16 little-endian operand
operand_primitives.summary: Read two unsigned bytes as a little-endian 16-bit value.
operand_primitives.description: Proven byte composition is `b0 | b1 << 8`; no signedness or mask is asserted here. Used for target PCs, string-table indices, and slot indices.

support.detail: OperandDescriptor width 2, little endian; JS VM operand separation supports this reader.

unknowns: The reference does not assert JavaScript signedness or masking for this reader beyond the proven byte composition.

operand_primitives.name: u24 little-endian operand
operand_primitives.summary: Read three unsigned bytes as a little-endian 24-bit value.
operand_primitives.description: Proven byte composition is `b0 | (b1 | b2 << 8) << 8`; no signedness or mask is asserted here. Used for target PCs and handler offsets.

support.detail: OperandDescriptor width 3, little endian; JS VM operand separation supports this reader.

unknowns: The reference does not assert JavaScript signedness or masking for this reader beyond the proven byte composition.

operand_primitives.name: PC advance by consumed operand bytes
operand_primitives.summary: Advance the bytecode PC by the exact number of operand bytes consumed.
operand_primitives.description: The source advances `context.byteOffset` (the proven PC field) once by the total operand width before using decoded operands. The advance is an effect, not an operand value.

support.detail: Operand separation records pc_delta; the symbolic tracer follows caller-supplied PC coordinates, not arbitrary handler PC writes.

unknowns: A source that captures the PC before or between operand reads is not covered by this primitive; operand separation declines such ordering.

primitives.name: Dispatch and state transition
primitives.summary: Select the next handler from the dispatch table and install the next state.
primitives.description: JavaScript VM: the dispatch method reads `vmDispatchTable[state][bytecode[pc++]]` and returns the selector, which reaches the proven operation table through an Oxc SymbolId join. WebAssembly VM: the interpreter reads a u8 opcode at the PC, indexes a memory-resident state/opcode table, uses the low byte as a `br_table` operand, and installs the high byte as the next state. The branch-to-handler join for the WebAssembly VM remains unproven.

support.detail: Complete dispatch and the JavaScript VM prefix prove a narrow dispatch topology. WebAssembly dispatch state selection is static evidence only; no WASM execution and no branch-to-handler join.

unknowns: The WebAssembly `br_table` case -> JavaScript handler key join is not established.

primitives.name: Direct operand jump
primitives.summary: Set PC and dispatch state from a target operand and a state byte.
primitives.description: The handler decodes a target PC and a next dispatch state, advances the PC past the operands, then assigns both context fields. Width variants are separate proven encodings, not one normalized width.

support.detail: The bounded graph/template extractor recognizes proven absolute PC and dispatch-state writes, and the symbolic tracer plus dispatch drivers follow u8, u16 and u24 target variants when decoded numeric operands and the caller-supplied cursor are available.

unknowns: The WebAssembly VM performs equivalent control transfer inside the interpreter, but no byte-equivalence proof or bounded WebAssembly execution is asserted.

primitives.name: Indirect jump through memory slots
primitives.summary: Read a PC and dispatch state from two memory slots and jump there.
primitives.description: Two u8 slot indices are decoded, the PC is advanced past them, then the state slot and PC slot are read from VM memory and installed. Source order places the two reads after the PC advance; the final assignment order is pc then state.

support.detail: The bounded extractor recognizes proven memory-slot PC/state reads and control writes; the symbolic tracer follows them when the slots contain concrete numeric VM coordinates.

unknowns: The target is followed only when both slots hold VM values; otherwise the reference requires a diagnostic rather than a guess.

primitives.name: Indirect jump through the stack
primitives.summary: Take PC and dispatch state from the top two stack values and pop both.
primitives.description: The old top becomes the PC and the old top-1 becomes the dispatch state; two stack slots are removed. No operand bytes are consumed.

support.detail: The bounded extractor recognizes the proven stack-held state/PC pair and its two-value pop; the symbolic tracer follows the transfer when the stack values are concrete numeric VM coordinates.

unknowns: The source does not guard an empty stack; that failure shape is not modeled here.

primitives.name: Conditional branch on truthiness
primitives.summary: Advance past a target/state pair, and jump only when the tested top value is truthy.
primitives.description: The tested value is the stack top. The source advances past the operands, conditionally writes PC/state when truthy, then pops one value. Program-value conditions are AST control decisions; VM-value conditions are followed concretely.

support.detail: The catalogue can record a `branch` action but does not identify this VM jump shape; the tracer does not yet execute it.

unknowns: Program-value and VM-value conditions require different handling; no current tracer path proves both.

primitives.name: Conditional branch on falsiness
primitives.summary: Advance past a target/state pair, and jump only when the tested top value is falsy.
primitives.description: The tested value is the stack top. The source advances past the operands, conditionally writes PC/state when falsy, then pops one value.

support.detail: Same boundary as the truthy branch.

unknowns: Program-value and VM-value conditions require different handling; no current tracer path proves both.

primitives.name: Branch when a memory slot is not null
primitives.summary: Jump when the value read from a memory slot is not null; do not pop.
primitives.description: The source reads a u8 slot, a u24 target and a u8 state, advances past all operands, reads the slot, and conditionally jumps without changing stack height.

support.detail: No current recognizer or execution support.

unknowns: The source performs a loose `!= null` comparison; both `null` and `undefined` are non-null outcomes and are not separated here.

primitives.name: Branch unless the stack top is less than a slot
primitives.summary: Pop one stack value and jump unless `top < readSlot(slot)`.
primitives.description: The source reads a u8 slot, a u24 target and a u8 state, advances, reads the slot and the stack top, computes `top < slot`, and jumps when the comparison is false; the tested value is popped.

support.detail: No current recognizer or execution support.

unknowns: JavaScript comparison semantics (coercion and possible throws) are preserved as opaque program values; no numeric-only assumption is made.

primitives.name: Direct VM call
primitives.summary: Push a return frame and transfer control to a target PC/state.
primitives.description: The handler decodes the target and next state, advances the PC, pushes `{returnByteOffset: pc after operands, returnDispatchState: current state}`, then installs the target/state. The WebAssembly VM relocates call dispatch to `call_indirect`/the guarded wrapper and does not keep a JavaScript frame.

support.detail: The bounded extractor recognizes the proven operand advance, call-frame push and target/state writes; the symbolic tracer and dispatch drivers follow the call when a numeric target/state and VM cursor are supplied.

unknowns: The WebAssembly VM call transport is relocated into the interpreter and is not proven byte-equivalent to the JavaScript frame form.

primitives.name: Guarded operation call
primitives.summary: Invoke a handler through a JavaScript try/catch wrapper, or through the WebAssembly guarded import.
primitives.description: The JavaScript VM wrapper calls `operation(context)` inside try/catch and delegates a thrown value to the exception handler. The WebAssembly VM uses a guarded host wrapper when the error-region depth is non-zero and a direct `call_indirect` otherwise. The wrapper arity is capture-specific and is not unified.

support.detail: The complete dispatch driver records thrown completions and the guarded-wrapper source is proven; try/finally frame semantics are not executed.

unknowns: Wrapper arity differs by capture; the fixed WebAssembly VM reference proves five positional operands and the supplementary fragment proves six. No unified arity is claimed.

primitives.name: Program-value call
primitives.summary: Invoke a JavaScript function value from a fused handler and keep the result as a program value.
primitives.description: A fused return handler reads a callee and three arguments from the stack, calls the callee with a fourth slot value, writes the result into an output slot, then performs a VM return. The callee is a program value, not a VM operation.

support.detail: The bounded HandlerIR recognizer models the exact unshadowed `Function.prototype.apply.call` form with a one-argument stack slice. The symbolic tracer emits a throwing call when that slice resolves to a known array; general/direct program-value calls remain outside the admitted subset.

unknowns: Receiver identity and arbitrary argument count/order remain source-specific; dynamic argument arrays stop with an explicit diagnostic, while the concrete executor rejects `StackSlice` and `Call` values.

primitives.name: Push a VM call frame
primitives.summary: Push the return PC and return dispatch state before transferring to a callee.
primitives.description: Frame fields are proven as `returnByteOffset` and `returnDispatchState`. The PC captured is the value after the operand advance in the observed call bodies.

support.detail: The bounded recipe and symbolic tracer model the exact returnByteOffset/returnDispatchState frame captured from the VM cursor, subject to the configured frame-depth bound.

unknowns: A frame captured before the operand advance is a different ordering and is not covered by this primitive.

primitives.name: Pop a VM call frame
primitives.summary: Pop the return PC and dispatch state before resuming the caller.
primitives.description: The source pops one frame and assigns PC/state from its fields. It does not guard an empty stack.

support.detail: The bounded recipe and symbolic tracer pop the most recent proven VM frame and restore its byte offset and dispatch state; an empty frame stack stops explicitly.

unknowns: An empty call-frame stack produces a source-level property read on `undefined`; that failure shape is not modeled as a semantic return.

primitives.name: Handler return
primitives.summary: Return from a handler to the dispatcher and resume from the top call frame.
primitives.description: A pure return pops the call frame and writes PC/state from it. Handler return is not the same event as VM completion; ordinary handler returns continue the run loop.

support.detail: The bounded extractor recognizes the VM frame-pop/resume shape and the symbolic tracer follows it with explicit empty-stack and depth/budget boundaries. An ordinary JavaScript handler return remains distinct from VM completion.

unknowns: Return value handling is not present in the pure-return body; value-return forms are fused and are represented separately.

primitives.name: Enter try
primitives.summary: Push a try frame with the handler PC, handler state and an error-entry count.
primitives.description: The handler decodes a handler PC and handler state, advances past them, and pushes `{handlerByteOffset, handlerDispatchState, errorEntryCount: 0}`.

support.detail: No current catalogue kind or tracer try-frame state.

unknowns: The observed source always creates `errorEntryCount` as 0 and nothing in the inspected bodies increments it; its unwind meaning is unresolved.

primitives.name: Exit try on the normal path
primitives.summary: Pop the active try frame after a try/catch body completes normally.
primitives.description: The body only pops `tryFrameStack`; it consumes no operands.

support.detail: No current tracer try-frame state.

unknowns: Whether a non-empty frame is guaranteed is not asserted by the source.

primitives.name: Enter finally on the normal path
primitives.summary: Save the resume PC/state in an error record and transfer to the finally handler.
primitives.description: The source pushes `{wasExceptionHandled: false, savedByteOffset: current pc, savedDispatchState: current state}`, pops the try frame, then writes PC/state from the popped handler fields.

support.detail: No current tracer error-record or try-frame state.

unknowns: The source saves the PC before the handler jump; whether this is always the post-opcode coordinate is not asserted beyond the observed body.

primitives.name: Catch and bind the thrown value
primitives.summary: Pop the error record, pop the pending thrown value, and write it to a memory slot.
primitives.description: The JavaScript VM form decodes a u8 slot, advances, pops the error record, pops the thrown value and writes the slot. The WebAssembly VM form receives the slot as a host-import operand and writes `errorStack.pop()` to it.

variants.note: The slot index is supplied by the interpreter to the host import; it is not read inline by the JavaScript handler.

support.detail: No current tracer exception-frame state.

unknowns: The raw thrown value is preserved as a program value; no wrapping or identity change is asserted.

primitives.name: Catch without a binding
primitives.summary: Pop the error record and drop the pending thrown value when it was handled.
primitives.description: The source pops one error record. It pops `thrownValueStack` only when `wasExceptionHandled` is true.

support.detail: No current tracer exception-frame state.

primitives.name: End finally
primitives.summary: Pop the error record and either rethrow the pending value or resume at the saved PC/state.
primitives.description: When the popped error record says an exception was handled, the source throws the pending thrown value. Otherwise it writes the saved PC/state and continues.

support.detail: The catalogue can record a throw action, but the tracer does not maintain the error-record stack.

primitives.name: Request WebAssembly unwind
primitives.summary: Set the interpreter's single mutable unwind-request flag.
primitives.description: When a VM throw occurs inside an active error region, the interpreter stores constant 1 into mutable global 0 and branches to the unwind cascade. The host catch wrapper also sets the same flag through the exported setter.

support.detail: No WebAssembly execution; the flag is static evidence only.

unknowns: The fixed WebAssembly VM reference and the other captured WebAssembly VM kernel have different setter/import names; no name unification is performed.

primitives.name: Resume after WebAssembly unwind
primitives.summary: Clear the unwind flag, restore saved PC/state and truncate the JavaScript error stack while preserving the pending top value.
primitives.description: At the loop tail the interpreter reads global 0. When set, it clears it, runs a bounded cascade over the error-region depth, restores PC/state locals, and calls the truncation import. The final `unreachable` guards a loop that never falls through.

support.detail: No WebAssembly execution and no recovered full unwind-frame layout.

unknowns: The complete save/restore frame layout is not recovered; only the flag, cascade shape and one truncation call are proven.

primitives.name: Rethrow the raw value
primitives.summary: Throw the pending raw value out of the WebAssembly frame without wrapping it.
primitives.description: The rethrow import body is exactly `throw context.errorStack.pop();`. The raw value crosses the WASM frame unchanged.

support.detail: The symbolic tracer records thrown completions, but it does not execute this WebAssembly host import.

unknowns: The raw value may be any JavaScript value, including objects, strings, numbers, `undefined` and functions.

primitives.name: Truncate the WebAssembly error stack keeping the top
primitives.summary: Drop a requested number of error-stack entries while preserving the pending top value.
primitives.description: The host import reads the top value, subtracts `operand1` from the array length, then restores the top at the new last index.

support.detail: No WebAssembly host-import execution.

unknowns: The meaning of `operand1` (error-region depth versus count) is read from the interpreter call site; this reference does not generalize it.

primitives.name: Completion selector sentinel
primitives.summary: Treat an explicit selector value as terminal rather than as a handler key, then produce the selected completion value.
primitives.description: The complete-dispatch driver requires a caller-supplied, source-validated selector. The terminal step consumes only the opcode byte, has no operands, and never invents a handler. The selector value is a per-capture contract, not a magic constant and not an operation identity.

support.detail: `CompletionContract::SelectorSentinel` is validated by `dispatch::prepare` and exercised by `dispatch::execute`; the selector is never inferred from a handler key.

unknowns: The selector value and value policy are caller-supplied per capture; this reference does not bless one numeric selector for all kernels.

primitives.name: Run-loop sentinel check
primitives.summary: Compare a completion register with an immutable not-complete sentinel before dispatch, and return the pending result when they differ.
primitives.description: The JavaScript VM run loop declares two uninitialized locals, initializes the completion register to an immutable sentinel, and at the top of each iteration returns the register and resets it when it differs from the sentinel. This is separate from the dispatch-table selector contract.

support.detail: The JavaScript VM prefix proof requires the immutable sentinel, the exact register initialization, and confined writes. The prefix driver stops at its first unsupported boundary instead of claiming completion.

unknowns: The completion register is written by return handlers; the complete mapping from each return form to the register value is not recovered.

primitives.name: Completion from the stack
primitives.summary: Produce the completion value by popping or reading the VM stack.
primitives.description: The WebAssembly VM run loop maps status 1 to `context.stack.pop()`. The dispatch API generalizes the read to a stack index; the source evidence only proves the top value for the inspected host loop.

support.detail: `CompletionValue::Stack { index }` is implemented; the source proves the top-of-stack form used by the inspected host loop.

unknowns: A non-top stack index is an API policy, not a source-proven default.

primitives.name: Completion without a value
primitives.summary: Produce an explicit `undefined` completion.
primitives.description: The WebAssembly VM run loop maps status 0 to a bare `return`, which is the source form of an explicit undefined completion value.

support.detail: `CompletionValue::Undefined` is an explicit caller policy, never a silent default.

primitives.name: Completion from the pending-result register
primitives.summary: Return the pending result register value and reset the register to the sentinel.
primitives.description: The JavaScript VM run loop returns the completion register, which return handlers can set. This is a third completion transport, distinct from selector-controlled stack completion and explicit undefined completion.

support.detail: The prefix proof recognizes the register convention but stops at the first boundary; complete dispatch has no register transport.

unknowns: The exact mapping from return handler forms to the pending-result register is not recovered.

primitives.name: WebAssembly interpreter status
primitives.summary: Return an i32 status 0 or 1 from the interpreter and map it to a completion.
primitives.description: The interpreter export returns status 1 at explicit value-completion sites and status 0 at explicit empty-completion sites. The JavaScript host loop switches on the status; no other status is produced by the inspected modules.

support.detail: No WebAssembly execution. The status values are static source evidence.

unknowns: Whether any other captured WebAssembly VM kernel produces additional status values is not claimed.

primitives.name: Capture a VM thread
primitives.summary: Build a thread invocation with captured memory slots, optional result-slot self reference, and a per-invocation memory clone.
primitives.description: The canonical helper copies each captured slot by reference into a fresh memory object, builds the invocation, and optionally initializes and writes the result slot to the invocation itself. The public thread API applies the same documented order from caller-supplied inputs.

support.detail: `DispatchPreparation::thread` applies the documented capture order from caller inputs; the descriptor and values are not source-proven.

unknowns: Live shared closure cells and receivers are rejected by the public API, not modeled.

primitives.name: Build a thread invocation closure
primitives.summary: Build the invocation closure that clones memory, constructs a context, applies arguments and initializes slots before running.
primitives.description: The closure clones the captured memory, constructs a `vmContext` with the invocation receiver, optionally writes the aggregate arguments slot, initializes initial slots, writes positional arguments, fills missing arguments with `undefined`, then calls the VM run loop.

support.detail: The thread API reproduces this order for caller-supplied descriptors and values.

unknowns: Receivers and live shared captures are unsupported; argument identity/ordering across captures remains caller-supplied.

primitives.name: Invoke a thread
primitives.summary: Invoke the built thread closure with positional arguments and return the VM result.
primitives.description: Invocation creates a fresh context per call, preserves the argument order, and returns the run-loop result. The public API accepts a bounded positional argument iterator.

support.detail: `ThreadInvocation::invoke` is implemented for caller-supplied descriptors, values and positional arguments.

unknowns: Receivers are rejected rather than silently dropped; live shared capture is unsupported.

composites.name: Decode-string property read, then call
composites.summary: Decode a string operand, read a property with it, then push a return frame and call.
composites.description: Operands are a u16 string key and a u24 target/state pair. The work reads the stack top, decodes `vmDecodeString(top, key)`, reads `top-1[name]`, pushes a call frame, transfers to the target and replaces `top-1` with the property result before popping one value.

support.detail: The bounded extractor recognizes the direct call/frame effects and the supported stack/property work, but the dynamic string-decoder call remains an explicit unsupported region; this composite is not admitted for execution.

unknowns: The decoder is treated as the proven shared decoder only when the helper identity is proven; the reference does not infer it from a name.

composites.name: String-table property read into a slot, then call
composites.summary: Read a string table entry, read a property, write it to a slot, then push a return frame and call.
composites.description: Operands are a u16 string index, a u8 slot, a u24 target and a u8 state. The work reads `vmStringTable[index]`, reads `top[name]`, writes the slot, pushes a frame, transfers, and pops one value.

support.detail: The bounded extractor and symbolic tracer cover the proven string-table/property read, slot write, stack update, call-frame push and direct target/state transfer when operands and symbolic inputs are supplied.

composites.name: Copy slot to slot, then call
composites.summary: Copy one memory slot to another, then push a return frame and call.
composites.description: Operands are a from-slot u8, a to-slot u8, a u24 target and a u8 state. The work reads the source slot, writes the destination slot, pushes a frame and transfers.

support.detail: The bounded extractor and symbolic tracer cover the proven slot read/write, call-frame push and direct target/state transfer in source order when operands and symbolic inputs are supplied.

composites.name: Store two stack values into slots, then call
composites.summary: Write the top two stack values to two slots, then push a return frame and call.
composites.description: Operands are two u8 slot indices, a u24 target and a u8 state. The work writes `top` to the first slot, `top-1` to the second slot, pushes a frame, transfers, and pops two values.

support.detail: The bounded extractor and symbolic tracer cover both stack reads, slot writes, stack truncation, call-frame push and direct target/state transfer in source order when operands and symbolic inputs are supplied.

composites.name: Define property, then call
composites.summary: Define a data property from three stack values, then push a return frame and call.
composites.description: Operands are a u8 immediate, a u24 target and a u8 state. The work calls `Object.defineProperty(top-2, top-1, {value: top, writable:true, configurable:true, enumerable:true})`, pushes a frame, transfers, and leaves `[object, immediate]` while popping one value.

support.detail: The direct call/frame effects are recognized, but `Object.defineProperty` is a dynamic helper call outside the bounded recipe subset, so this composite remains inadmissible for execution.

unknowns: The define-property descriptor is fixed in the observed body; no other descriptor shape is claimed.

composites.name: Push two slots, then call
composites.summary: Push two memory-slot values and then transfer through a call frame.
composites.description: Two operand encodings are proven: a u16 first slot with a u8 second slot, and two u8 slots. Both push the slot values at the old stack length without popping, push a call frame, and transfer.

support.detail: The bounded extractor and symbolic tracer cover both proven slot reads, stack appends, call-frame push and direct target/state transfer for both operand-width variants.

unknowns: The two operand encodings are kept as variants; they are not normalized to one width.

composites.name: Store top into a slot, then call
composites.summary: Write the stack top to a memory slot, then push a return frame and call.
composites.description: Operands are a u8 slot, a u24 target and a u8 state. The work reads the top, writes the slot, pushes a frame, transfers, and rewrites the top with the same value (the source preserves stack height).

support.detail: The bounded extractor and symbolic tracer cover the proven slot write, stack preservation, call-frame push and direct target/state transfer in source order.

composites.name: Push two immediates, then call
composites.summary: Push two u8 immediates, then push a return frame and call.
composites.description: Operands are two u8 immediates, a u24 target and a u8 state. The work pushes both immediates at the old stack length, pushes a frame and transfers.

support.detail: The bounded extractor and symbolic tracer cover the proven immediate stack appends, call-frame push and direct target/state transfer in source order.

composites.name: Decode top as a string and push a slot, then call
composites.summary: Replace the stack top with a decoded string, push a slot value, then push a return frame and call.
composites.description: Operands are a u16 string key, a u8 slot, a u24 target and a u8 state. The work decodes the top, reads the slot, pushes a frame, transfers, replaces the top with the decoded string and appends the slot value.

support.detail: The direct call/frame effects and slot read are recognized, but the dynamic string-decoder call remains unsupported, so this composite is not admitted for execution.

composites.name: Replace top with a slot, then call
composites.summary: Replace the stack top with a memory-slot value, then push a return frame and call.
composites.description: Operands are a u8 slot, a u24 target and a u8 state. The work reads the slot, pushes a frame, transfers, and overwrites the top.

support.detail: The bounded extractor and symbolic tracer cover the proven slot read, call-frame push, direct target/state transfer and top replacement in source order.

composites.name: Property write, then call
composites.summary: Write a stack value to a property, replace the object with a slot value, then push a return frame and call.
composites.description: Operands are a u8 slot, a u24 target and a u8 state. The work performs `(top-2)[top-1] = top` in strict mode, reads the slot, pushes a frame, transfers, replaces `top-2` with the slot value, and pops two values.

support.detail: The bounded extractor and symbolic tracer cover the proven strict property write, slot read, call-frame push, direct target/state transfer and stack collapse in source order.

composites.name: Store top into a slot and load another, then call
composites.summary: Write the top to one slot, read another slot into the top, then push a return frame and call.
composites.description: Operands are a write-slot u8, a read-slot u8, a u24 target and a u8 state. The work writes the top, reads the second slot, pushes a frame, transfers and overwrites the top with the read value.

support.detail: The bounded extractor and symbolic tracer cover the proven slot write/read, call-frame push, direct target/state transfer and top replacement in source order.

composites.name: Property read by byte key, then call
composites.summary: Read a property with a u8 key, then push a return frame and call.
composites.description: Operands are a u8 key, a u24 target and a u8 state. The work reads `top[key]`, pushes a frame, transfers and replaces the top.

support.detail: The bounded extractor and symbolic tracer cover the proven byte-key property read, call-frame push, direct target/state transfer and top replacement in source order.

composites.name: Property read by string-table key, then call
composites.summary: Read a property whose name comes from the string table, then push a return frame and call.
composites.description: Operands are a u16 string index, a u24 target and a u8 state. The work reads `vmStringTable[index]`, reads `top[name]`, pushes a frame, transfers and replaces the top.

support.detail: The bounded extractor and symbolic tracer cover the proven string-table/property read, call-frame push, direct target/state transfer and top replacement in source order.

composites.name: Push an immediate and a slot, then call
composites.summary: Push a u8 immediate and a memory-slot value, then push a return frame and call.
composites.description: Operands are a u8 immediate, a u8 slot, a u24 target and a u8 state. The work pushes the immediate and the slot value at the old stack length, pushes a frame and transfers.

support.detail: The bounded extractor and symbolic tracer cover the proven immediate/slot stack appends, call-frame push and direct target/state transfer in source order.

composites.name: Call a program function, then return
composites.summary: Call a program callee with stack arguments, write the result to a slot, then pop the frame and return.
composites.description: Operands are a u8 slot and a u8 output slot. The work reads the slot, calls `top-3(top-2, top-1, top, slot)`, writes the result to the output slot, pops the frame, resumes the caller and pops four stack values.

support.detail: The frame-pop/resume effects are recognized, but the dynamic program-value call is outside the bounded recipe subset, so this composite is not admitted for execution.

unknowns: The callee is a program value; receiver identity and possible throw are preserved as program semantics, not a VM operation.

composites.name: Push two slots, then return
composites.summary: Read two slots, push their values, then pop the frame and return.
composites.description: Operands are two u8 slots. The work reads both slots, pops the frame, resumes the caller, then pushes both values at the old stack length.

support.detail: The bounded extractor and symbolic tracer cover the proven slot reads, frame pop/resume and stack appends in source order when operands and a caller frame are supplied.

composites.name: Define property and push a decoded string, then return
composites.summary: Define a data property, decode a string into the result position, then pop the frame and return.
composites.description: Operands are a u16 string index and a u16 XOR key. The work defines a data property from the top three stack values, decodes the string-table entry, pops the frame, resumes the caller, and leaves `[object, decoded_string]` while popping one value.

support.detail: The frame-pop/resume effects are recognized, but `Object.defineProperty` and the dynamic string decoder remain outside the bounded recipe subset.

composites.name: Push a slot and a decoded string, then return
composites.summary: Read a slot, decode a string, push both, then pop the frame and return.
composites.description: Operands are a u8 slot, a u16 string index and a u16 XOR key. The work reads the slot, decodes `vmDecodeString(strings[index], key)`, pops the frame, resumes the caller and pushes both values.

support.detail: The frame-pop/resume effects and slot read are recognized, but the dynamic string-decoder call remains outside the bounded recipe subset.

composites.name: String-table property read, then return
composites.summary: Read a property by a string-table name, then pop the frame and return.
composites.description: Operands are a u16 string index. The work reads `vmStringTable[index]`, reads `top[name]`, pops the frame, resumes the caller and replaces the top.

support.detail: The bounded extractor and symbolic tracer cover the proven string-table/property read, frame pop/resume and top replacement in source order when operands and a caller frame are supplied.

composites.name: XOR property write, then return
composites.summary: XOR the stack top with a u8 mask, write it to a property, then pop the frame and return.
composites.description: Operands are a u8 mask. The work computes `top ^ mask`, writes `(top-2)[top-1]`, pops the frame, resumes the caller and pops three values.

support.detail: The bounded extractor and symbolic tracer cover the proven XOR/property write, frame pop/resume and stack collapse in source order when the caller frame is supplied.

support_gaps: Conditional branches, loops and dynamic control-flow regions remain unsupported; bounded direct/indirect jumps, direct calls, call frames, VM returns and 15 fused composites are supported only with proven operands and caller-supplied VM state.

Dynamic decoder/helper calls, direct or arbitrary program-value calls outside the bounded apply-call proof, Object.defineProperty forms and possible-throw guarded calls remain outside the admitted recipe subset; concrete executor support for abstract program calls remains absent.
Try/catch/finally frame execution and the complete unwind frame layout are not implemented or fully recovered.
The WebAssembly branch-to-handler join, per-handler WebAssembly operand widths and WebAssembly execution remain unresolved.
The JavaScript VM pending-result completion register is not mapped into the complete-dispatch completion contract.
Thread descriptors and incoming thread values are caller-supplied; live shared captures and receivers are rejected.
No JavaScript or WebAssembly runtime execution is performed or claimed.

non_claims: This reference does not claim coverage of every handler in any kernel or of unseen kernels.
It does not claim byte-level semantic equivalence between the JavaScript VM and WebAssembly VM placements.
It does not execute captured JavaScript or WebAssembly, and it does not derive runtime facts such as taken branches or thrown-value identity.
It does not bless a numeric completion selector, a handler key, a site name or a table position as operation identity.
It does not claim that the fixed WebAssembly VM snapshot reproduces the supplementary capture fragment.
It does not fabricate operand widths, signedness or masking beyond the proven source compositions.
It does not recover the complete WebAssembly unwind-frame layout or the WebAssembly branch-to-handler join.
unresolved: The WebAssembly dispatch branch -> JavaScript handler key join remains unproven.
Per-handler WebAssembly operand widths and the full unwind-frame layout remain unrecovered.
The semantics of `errorEntryCount` in the JavaScript VM try frame are unresolved; observed sources always create it as 0.
The exact mapping from each fused return form to the pending-result register is not recovered.

Receiver identity, arbitrary/direct program-value calls, dynamic decoder/helper calls and Object.defineProperty execution are not modeled; only bounded symbolic apply-calls with known stack arguments are emitted.
The fixed kernel snapshot paths are pinned, but their bytes are not embedded here; citations identify fragments by digest and document evidence.
No coverage of unseen kernels is claimed.
